consequence.statement: No operational consequence: operators only gain a new opt-in option — writing validation rules with assertion trees; the evidence describes no failure, rejection, ignored setting, or change to existing policies or workloads.

assertion.statement: Kyverno 1.13 adds the ability to use assertion trees (previously CLI-only, from Kyverno-JSON) as a sub-type of validation rules, so Kyverno policies can also validate non-Kubernetes workloads; the evidence names no schema field for this capability and describes no impact on existing behavior.

proposal.undeterminedReason: subject: The evidence (release-notes blog) announces the capability — assertion trees usable as a sub-type of validation rules — but neither the text nor the rendered-diff evidence names the concrete schema field (no path under spec.rules[].validate for assertion trees appears anywhere, and no ARTIFACT CONTEXT is given), so the exact crd-field identity cannot be pinned.; applicability: Exposure is not expressible as environment state: this is a new opt-in authoring capability; no existing configuration, resource, or workload state is named as touched, and the exact subject field (the assertion-tree sub-type under validation rules) is not identified in the evidence.
